A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CViT research work. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original CViT benchmark results and ablations, including Tables 2–3 and 5–6 and Figures 4 and 9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds compressible-flow evaluation, further ablations, attention analyses, and inference timings.

M1.justification: The encoder, Perceiver temporal aggregation, grid embedding, cross-attention decoder, and training objective are retained. v3 generalizes the latent-query notation and tests different query counts, while Appendix F.5 explicitly retains one query in the main implementation; this does not establish a replacement of the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds PDEBench compressible Navier–Stokes evaluation involving variable density, velocity, and pressure (Table 3 and Appendix F.6). This substantially extends the physical task coverage beyond v2's advection, shallow-water, incompressible-flow, and diffusion-reaction tasks, all of which remain.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds an inference-time comparison against ViT, FNO, and a model labeled UNet; ViT was not an evaluated comparator in v2. Existing accuracy comparator sets remain unchanged, and the new compressible-flow comparison uses existing Table 3 methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds controlled Fourier-frequency and latent-query sweeps, a compressible-flow setup with 9,000 training and 1,000 test trajectories, and batch-32 A6000 inference benchmarking. Existing benchmark protocols remain largely intact. The incompressible-flow dataset total changes from 7,900 to 7,800, matching the unchanged 6,500/1,300 split; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds Fourier-feature frequency sensitivity on shallow water (Table 7), temporal latent-query sensitivity on incompressible flow (Table 8), and encoder/decoder attention analyses (Figures 11–12). These substantially extend the questions investigated beyond v2's retained patch-size, embedding, grid-resolution, latent-width, and attention-head studies.

E5.justification: The new inference-time comparison explicitly averages measurements over 100 runs (Table 10). v2 provides no corresponding repetition information. This concerns timing measurements, not repeated model training; training-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and training-time entries are retained. New results include CNS error of 1.29% for CViT-L versus 1.31% for fine-tuned DPOT-L, Fourier-frequency results, and CViT-L/16 errors decreasing from 6.56% to 3.18% when queries increase from one to six. Table 10 adds inference times of 79.09 ms for CViT-L, 45.49 for ViT, 34.96 for FNO, and 44.25 for UNet.

T1.justification: Appendix F.6 adds the formal compressible Navier–Stokes system and associated physical definitions, including Equations 59–61. The conditioned-field analysis, FNO proposition, and Lipschitz theorems and proofs remain unchanged apart from numbering. The relative-L2 denominator's j-to-k correction is notational.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and discussion retain the same claims about CViT's architecture, continuous querying, coordinate-embedding insights, and parameter-efficient benchmark performance. The new experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 proposes that single-query aggregation discards useful trajectory information and explains the accuracy–token-count tradeoff. It also interprets temporal recency and spatial locality in attention as physically meaningful behavior (Appendix F.5). Existing scalability, data-scarcity, and geometry limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 describes supplementary ablation code and a planned full release; v3 states that all code and data are public and supplies a concrete repository address. v3 also identifies CViT-B as the backbone for existing appendix ablations and documents settings for the new compressible-flow and timing experiments. These substantially expand the reported access and reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The reference lists contain the same works, and the detailed positioning against OFormer, GNOT, DPOT, and MPP is retained. Section 2 reorganizes the existing background and challenges without substantively changing the novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Section 2 gains Background, Transformer-Based Operator Learning, and Open Challenges subheadings, and the temporal-aggregation explanation is expanded. Publication headers, acknowledgments, terminology, and cross-references receive targeted edits; most existing prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table 3 with a CNS column and adds ablation and timing tables, compressible-flow figures, and attention visualizations. Existing rollout figures gain time-step labels, and the architecture diagram's tensor labels change. v2's diffusion-reaction Figures 6 and 13 become appendix Figures 18–19. Together these additions and display revisions substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens an already substantial evaluation through compressible-flow testing, controlled ablations, attention analyses, and transparent inference timings, while improving code/data access information. The timing results usefully expose a computational tradeoff. The gains are limited by incomplete timing configuration details and the erroneous 'activator and inhibitor' wording in the new compressible-flow setup. The core method, established results, and theoretical analysis remain essentially unchanged.
